gist: Transport for London was fined £2m following a fatal bus station collision.
The Health and Safety Executive found safety failures at Walthamstow bus station.
TfL pleaded guilty to breaching workplace health and safety regulations.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Grace Mecaley, a 74-year-old retired nurse, was killed after being struck by a double-decker bus at Walthamstow bus station on 15 December 2023. An investigation by the Health and Safety Executive determined that Transport for London failed to ensure safe circulation for pedestrians and vehicles. At Westminster Magistrates' Court, TfL pleaded guilty to breaching health and safety regulations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlights critical safety failings at a public transport hub. The court imposed a £2m fine on TfL, reflecting the severity of the breach and the tragic loss of life. The case serves as a reminder of the responsibility organisations hold for public safety within their managed environments.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: TfL has stated it is considering its next steps regarding the fine amount. Additionally, the organisation completed works to permanently improve pedestrian safety at the Walthamstow site in December 2024.
